answer: Retrospective Co-Activity Clustering. Log each identity's transactions into a shared atlas of interaction graphs, then run community detection to flag dense clusters of new identities that transact mainly with each other. A cluster whose internal edge rate exceeds a nebula of organic peers by a set threshold is quarantined and its rewards clawed back. To evade, an attacker must forge sustained, costly interactions with unrelated honest agents, paying real fees and risking detection per identity.
